privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: Padiush stores ethnobotanical research data: interviews, audio recordings, photographs and field locations. This policy explains what we collect, why, where it lives and what control you have over it. We do not sell data, we do not use it for advertising, and we do not train artificial intelligence models on it.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are and what this policy covers

blocks.text: Padiush is operated by Mercedes Menéndez and Rodrigo Arévalo, as individuals, from El Salvador. We act as joint controllers of user account data.
This policy covers the padiushbio.com website, the web platform and the Padiush Companion mobile app. You can write to us at any time at the address given at the end.

sections.heading: 2. Two kinds of data, two responsibilities

blocks.text: The most important distinction in this policy is who answers for each kind of information.

items.text: we are the controller. This is what we need to give you access and to communicate with you.

the researcher is the controller. This covers interview answers, audio, photographs, location and any personal data about the people interviewed. We act as a processor and handle that information on the researcher's instructions.

blocks.text: Whoever leads a study is responsible for obtaining informed consent from the people interviewed and any applicable ethics approvals. We do not access the contents of a study unless it is strictly necessary to provide support you have requested, to restore information, or to comply with a legal obligation.

items.text: name, email address, password (stored as an irreversible hash, never in plain text), email verification status, language and visual theme.
title, institution, country, authorship, team members, assigned roles and invitations.
interview forms, recorded answers, the species catalog and names exactly as they were reported in the field.
capture date and time, GPS coordinates when the device provides them, audio recordings and photographs.
only what the researcher chooses to record in their forms.
the name you give a device and a per-device access token for the mobile app.
your name, email address and the message you send us.
our server keeps ordinary access logs (IP address, browser, date and requested resource) for a short period, for security and diagnostics.

sections.heading: 4. What we use the information for

blocks.text: We use your data only to make the platform work: creating and authenticating your account, syncing captures made on mobile, calculating the ethnobiological indices, generating your exports, sending necessary emails (verification, password reset, invitations and replies to the contact form) and protecting the service from abuse.
We do not sell or rent your information. We do not use it for advertising or to build commercial profiles. We do not train artificial intelligence models on your data or on interview content.
To understand how the platform is used we run Umami, an analytics tool hosted on our own infrastructure. Usage data does not go to an external analytics provider.

Umami sets no cookies, creates no persistent identifiers and cannot follow you across other sites. It does not store your IP address: it uses it transiently to derive an approximate location and an anonymous identifier that is renewed daily. It also honours your browser's Do Not Track signal.
The only cookies we use are necessary for the service to work:

items.text: keeps you signed in.
protects forms against forged requests.
remembers the language you chose.

blocks.text: Your light or dark theme preference is kept in your browser's local storage, not in a cookie.
We do not share your information with third parties for their own purposes. Only the providers needed to run the service are involved:

items.text: hosting, database, file storage and encrypted backups, on servers located in the United States.
delivery of the platform's transactional email.

blocks.text: Within the platform, a project's information is visible to the people its owner has invited, according to the role assigned to them. We would only hand information to an authority where the law requires it.

To help you identify species we query World Flora Online, GBIF (which publishes Kew's World Checklist of Vascular Plants) and iNaturalist. These queries carry plant names only: we never send personal data, interview answers, field locations or your account identifiers.

iNaturalist reference photographs are served through our own server. Your browser never contacts iNaturalist directly, so your IP address is not exposed to that service. We do not store those images: they are displayed at the moment of viewing, credited to their author, with their licence and a link to the source.

We do not currently transcribe interview recordings. If we enable that feature, processing will run on infrastructure under our control: audio will not be sent to third-party transcription services, and we will tell you before it is switched on.

sections.heading: 9. Where data is kept and how it is protected

blocks.text: Information is hosted on Amazon Web Services servers in the United States. If you are based elsewhere, this means an international transfer of data; by using the platform you accept that transfer, which we protect with the technical measures described below.

items.text: all communication is encrypted with HTTPS/TLS.
interview answers and transcriptions are encrypted at the application level.
audio and photographs are kept in access-restricted object storage, reachable only through signed links with a limited lifetime.
permissions are checked per project and per role on every request, from both the web and the mobile app.

the local database is encrypted with SQLCipher using a key generated on the device itself and held in the system keychain. Photographs and recordings are encrypted too, unencrypted originals are deleted once ingested, and content is removed from the phone once the server confirms it was stored. If encryption is unavailable the app refuses to capture rather than saving anything unprotected. Your password is never stored on the device.

we take a full backup daily and archive the transaction log every hour. Both are encrypted with managed keys, protected against deletion for their retention period, and their restoration has been tested. We keep full backups for 400 days and transaction logs for 45 days.

blocks.text: No system is completely secure and we cannot guarantee absolute protection. If we detected unauthorised access to your information, we would contact you to explain what happened and how we are resolving it.
We keep your account and research data for as long as the account exists. When you delete a project or ask us to delete your account, the information is removed from the active systems.

After that deletion, data may remain in our encrypted backups for up to 400 days, after which it expires automatically. We do not use those backups for anything other than restoring the service after an incident.

Wherever you live, we grant you the following rights over your personal data: access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, objection, portability and withdrawal of consent. You may also lodge a complaint with your relevant data protection authority.
Several of these rights are already built into the platform: you can view and correct your data from your account, export your research information as CSV or XLSX, and delete the projects you own.

Deleting a whole account is currently handled on request: write to us and we will process it. For any other request, contact us using the details at the end of this policy; we will respond within 30 days at the latest.

The platform is intended for researchers over the age of 18 and we do not create accounts for anyone younger. If a study involves minors as interviewees, it is for whoever leads the study to obtain the necessary consents and authorisations.
If we change this policy we will let you know by email at least 30 days before the changes take effect, so you have time to review them.
Write to us if you have questions about this policy or want to exercise any of your rights:

terms.title: Terms and conditions
terms.summary: Padiush is a research platform in beta. You keep ownership of your data and your research; we keep ownership of the software. These terms explain what we expect from you and what you can expect from us.

blocks.text: These terms govern your access to and use of Padiush, both the web platform and the Padiush Companion mobile app. By creating an account and using the platform, you accept them. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.
You must be over 18 and register with accurate details. Access is currently by invitation and requires verifying your email address.

Your account is personal and non-transferable. You are responsible for keeping your credentials confidential and for activity that happens under your account. Tell us immediately if you suspect unauthorised use.
Padiush is under active development. Features may change, and in some cases be withdrawn, and interruptions or errors may occur. We do not guarantee uninterrupted availability or freedom from faults.
For that reason we recommend using the export feature regularly and keeping your own copies of research information that matters to you.
In using the platform, you agree not to:

items: Upload unlawful content, content that infringes copyright, or material that is offensive or defamatory.
Reverse-engineer the software, or copy, modify or distribute it without our permission.
Access information that is not yours, circumvent access controls, or exploit faults to obtain other people's data.
Use the platform to harass others or for unlawful activity.
Interfere with the operation of the service or its infrastructure.

blocks.text: If you discover a vulnerability or accidentally reach information that is not yours, you must report it to us immediately and must not disclose or exploit it.
Padiush holds information about real people and about traditional knowledge. By recording data on the platform you confirm that:

items: You have obtained informed consent from the people interviewed, including specific consent to record audio and take photographs where you do so.
You hold any ethics or institutional approvals your research requires.
You comply with applicable obligations regarding traditional knowledge, including community agreements and any access and benefit-sharing rules that apply.
You have a valid legal basis for processing the personal data you record.

blocks.text: In respect of that information you act as the controller and we act as the processor. We may suspend access to content that manifestly breaches these conditions.
You keep ownership of the information and content you upload: your projects, forms, answers, catalogs, recordings and images are yours.

So that we can provide the service, you grant us a limited, non-exclusive and revocable licence to host, back up, process and display that content, solely in order to operate the platform for you and for the people you invite. We do not use your content for any other purpose.
The Padiush software, its design and its brand belong to us. You may not copy, modify, distribute or create derivative works from them without our written permission.

The platform queries World Flora Online, GBIF (World Checklist of Vascular Plants) and iNaturalist to help you identify species and see their distribution. That information belongs to its respective sources and is subject to their own terms and licences.

iNaturalist reference photographs remain the property of the people who took them and are governed by the licence shown beside each image. If you want to reuse them in a publication, check that licence and respect the corresponding credits.

The ethnobiological indices, taxonomic matches and distribution maps the platform offers are calculation and reference tools, not scientific determinations. External sources may contain errors or be out of date.
Before publishing, verify the results, the identifications and the citations. Scientific responsibility for a publication always rests with the person who signs it.
We work to keep the platform secure and available, but the service is provided "as is", with no warranties beyond those required by law.

To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for accidental loss of information, for service interruptions, or for indirect damages or loss of profit arising from the use of, or inability to use, the platform. Nothing in these terms excludes liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

If we detect a breach of these terms we may suspend or delete your account and prevent new accounts from being created. Unless the law prevents it, we will tell you about the situation and give you the opportunity to explain your side before taking a final measure. In the case of deliberate breaches we may pursue the legal remedies available to us.
You may stop using the platform whenever you wish and ask for your account to be deleted as described in the privacy policy.
If we amend these terms we will tell you by email at least 30 days before the changes take effect. If you keep using the platform after that date, we will take it that you accept the new version.
These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of El Salvador. Any dispute relating to them will be resolved before the courts of the city of San Salvador.
